blockingLoop.evidence: Second turn repeats the first almost verbatim: "Drying sends fluff and condensed water out through the pump, so a clogged pump filter at the bottom front stops drying... Was the filter full of fluff or debris" despite the customer asking "Is that likely to cause no heat though?"

rationale: The assistant opened with an irrelevant pump-filter check for a no-heat symptom and then repeated it word-for-word while ignoring the customer's direct question about why a filter would stop heating. It never asked for the full model number, never asked about the interrupted drying cycle (the key clue), and never mentioned the thermal cut-out or lint/airflow blockage. The final turn did land on the right component area (drying heater or its thermostat) and sensibly escalated to an engineer without recommending parts or unsafe DIY, so the ending is safe and broadly correct, but the route was wasteful and under-diagnosed.
